packages.name: Launch Kit
packages.oneLiner: Everything a brand-new business needs to look established on day one.
packages.summary: A compact launch bundle: positioning, a logo lockup, brand colours and type, and a first month of social templates. You walk away with a brand that looks like it has been around for years.
deliverables: A one-page positioning note — who you are for, what you promise, and the words to say it in.
Primary logo plus stacked and icon variants, supplied as SVG, PNG and PDF.
A colour palette and type pairing with hex codes and usage rules.
Twelve editable Canva templates covering posts, stories and a cover image.
A short handover call and a written cheat sheet so your team can keep it consistent.
packages.who: Founders in their first year who need to look credible before they can afford a brand agency.
faq: How many logo revisions are included?
Two rounds of revisions on the chosen direction. In practice most clients sign off on round one.
Do I own the files?
Yes — full commercial rights transfer to you on final payment, including the source files.

packages.name: Growth Engine
packages.oneLiner: A content machine that keeps publishing whether or not you have a good week.
packages.summary: Twelve pieces of content a month across the channels that actually move for you, planned a month ahead so nothing is written in a panic on a Friday afternoon.
deliverables: A month-ahead calendar agreed with you before anything is written.
Twelve finished pieces — short-form posts, one long-form article, and the graphics to carry them.
Scheduling and publishing handled on your accounts, so nothing sits in a draft folder.
A plain-English monthly report: what ran, what landed, what we are changing next month.
A standing 30-minute monthly review call.
packages.who: Businesses that know they should be publishing consistently and have quietly stopped.
faq: Is there a minimum term?
Three months, because content needs a run-up before the numbers mean anything. After that it is month to month.
Who approves the content?
You do. Everything sits in a shared board for approval before it goes anywhere near a publish button.

packages.name: Paid Ads Sprint
packages.oneLiner: Six weeks to find out which ad actually sells the thing.
packages.summary: A structured test of audiences, hooks and landing copy across Meta and Google, run properly with a clean measurement setup, so at the end you know what to spend money on.
deliverables: Pixel, conversion and GA4 setup checked and fixed before a cent is spent.
Three audience sets against three creative angles — nine combinations, tested in sequence.
A rewrite of the landing page headline, subhead and call to action to match the winning angle.
Weekly one-page report: spend, cost per result, and the decision taken that week.
A closing document naming the winning combination and the budget to scale it at.
packages.who: Anyone who has boosted a post, seen nothing happen, and wants it done with a method.
faq: Does the price include ad spend?
No — spend is paid directly to Meta and Google from your own account so you keep the data and the history. Budget from $20 a day is enough to learn something.
What if nothing works?
Then you have saved yourself a year of guessing. The closing document says so plainly and recommends where to look instead.

packages.name: Local Visibility
packages.oneLiner: Be the business that comes up when someone nearby searches for what you sell.
packages.summary: Google Business Profile built out properly, local listings made consistent, review flow set up, and the on-page work that makes the map pack notice you.
deliverables: Google Business Profile claimed, categorised, described, and filled with photos and services.
Twenty directory listings created or corrected so your name, address and phone match everywhere.
A review request flow — QR card, SMS wording and a short follow-up sequence.
One optimised local landing page with schema markup and embedded map.
A ranking snapshot before and 30 days after, so the change is visible.
packages.who: Trades, clinics, salons, restaurants — anyone whose customers are within driving distance.
faq: Will I rank number one?
Nobody can promise a position. What this does is remove every reason Google has to overlook you, which is the part that is actually in our control.
Do you need access to my Google account?
Yes, as a manager on the Business Profile. You stay the owner and can remove access at any time.

packages.name: Conversion Rebuild
packages.oneLiner: Same traffic, more enquiries. We fix the page, not the budget.
packages.summary: A full teardown and rebuild of your main landing page or sales page — structure, copy, proof, and the mechanics of the form itself — against what the session recordings actually show people doing.
deliverables: Two weeks of heatmap and session recording, summarised into where people hesitate and leave.
A complete copy rewrite: headline, structure, objections, proof and call to action.
The rebuilt page, coded and live, loading in under two seconds on mobile.
A 30-day A/B test against the old page with a clear winner at the end.
The research document, so the same thinking can be applied to your other pages.
packages.who: Businesses already getting visitors who cannot work out why so few of them get in touch.
faq: What if my site is on Wix or Squarespace?
Fine. The rebuild is done inside whatever platform you already use, unless you would rather move — in which case say so up front.
How is the winner decided?
On enquiries or sales, never on clicks. The test runs until the difference is real or until 30 days, whichever comes first.

packages.name: Full Funnel
packages.oneLiner: Brand, content, ads and follow-up running as one system, reported in one place.
packages.summary: Our retained engagement. We own the whole path from first impression to signed customer, with a single dashboard and one person accountable for the number at the bottom of it.
deliverables: A quarterly plan with named targets, reviewed and reset every three months.
All content, paid campaigns and email handled in one calendar rather than three.
Lead capture and follow-up automated so nobody who enquires goes unanswered.
A live dashboard you can open any day of the week without asking us for a number.
A fortnightly call with the person doing the work, not an account manager.
packages.who: Established businesses spending money on marketing in four different places with no single view of it.
faq: Is this instead of hiring in-house?
For most businesses under about twenty staff, yes — and considerably cheaper. Past that it works best alongside one internal marketer.
Minimum term?
Six months. Funnel work compounds and anything shorter is not a fair test of it.
How do I pay?
Every package page has a direct payment link. You click it, pay by card on a secure hosted checkout, and we are notified immediately. No invoices to chase, no cart to fight with.
What happens straight after I pay?
You get a confirmation receipt and a short intake form within a few minutes. Work starts as soon as that comes back — usually the same working day.
Can I combine packages?
Yes, and most clients do. Pay for them separately or ask for a combined link if you would rather make one payment.
Are these prices final?
The listed price is what you pay. If something about your business genuinely sits outside the scope, we say so before taking money, not after.
Do you work with my industry?
Almost certainly. The packages are built around how buying decisions get made, which varies far less between industries than people expect.
Can I get a refund?
If we have not started, yes, in full. Once work is underway we would rather fix the thing you are unhappy with — that has always worked out better for both sides.
